sector_model: Fee and custodial platform: HSA assets and members, custodial yield, interest rate sensitivity, SBC and acquired amortization
thesis: HealthEquity (Nasdaq: HQY), largest HSA custodian: 10.7M HSAs (+8%), 37.9B assets (+14%). Fiscal Q2 FY2027 (quarter to 2026-07-31; 10-Q 0001428336-26-000041 filed 2026-08-27; release Ex99.1 of 8-K 0001428336-26-000040). Revenue 350.7M (+8%): service 124.4M, custodial 175.9M, interchange 50.4M; net income 65.6M (+10%), GAAP EPS 0.78, adjusted EBITDA 167.0M. FY2027 guidance (year to 2027-01-31) raised: revenue 1.411-1.421B, GAAP EPS 2.88-2.96, adjusted EBITDA 628-636M, non-GAAP EPS 4.66-4.73 (about 84M diluted shares); non-GAAP adds back 104M amortization and 87M SBC. TTM (FY ended 2026-01-31 + H1 FY27 - H1 FY26, XBRL): revenue 1,362M, net income 236.5M, OCF 490.2M, capex 53.2M (PP&E 2.5M plus capitalized software 50.8M), FCF 437.0M. Shares 82.715M (10-Q cover 2026-08-20), market cap about 8.56B at 103.46: TTM P/E 36.2x, 35.4x on GAAP guide midpoint 2.92, 22.0x on non-GAAP guide; FCF yield 5.1%, about 4.1% after FY27 SBC outlook of 87M; EV about 9.2B (cash 256.0M, long term debt 931.1M) or 14.6x adjusted EBITDA guide. Buybacks 231.1M in H1 FY27, 948.4M authorization remains. Market view: a steady compounder whose custodial income depends on rates and sweep economics. Evidence for: member and asset growth, raised guide, cash conversion. Gap closing: sustained 8-10% revenue growth with margin expansion as the next quarter reports (fiscal Q3 expected early December, date unverified).
counterthesis: Custodial revenue (50% of total) is tied to interest rates and the yield HealthEquity earns on cash held at partner banks; lower rates or worse sweep terms cut it directly, and the stock is priced at 35x GAAP earnings. GAAP earnings carry 104M of acquired intangible amortization from the WageWorks deal, so non-GAAP flatters but SBC of 87M is a real cost. Debt of 931M (about 1.5x adjusted EBITDA) is modest but buybacks of 231M in six months exceeded free cash flow after SBC. Competitors (Fidelity, banks, Lively, employers' platforms) and regulatory change to HSA rules or interchange could compress fees. A 5.02 officer-change 8-K of 2026-10-09 is unread. MD&A, risk factors and debt covenants were not read, peers (Paylocity-style HR/benefit processors, WEX, Fidelity) not compared, and the customer concentration in partner banks is unverified.
invalidation: Thesis fails if custodial yield falls faster than asset growth, HSA member growth slows below about 5%, free cash flow stops covering buybacks, or regulation or partner bank terms reduce custodial economics.
